title: 184. UNHEALTHY RELATIONSHIPS: Red Flags & Risk Factors in Teen Relationships feat. Eden Garcia-Balis
description_html: Today's guest is Eden Garcia-Balis— a licensed Marriage and Family Therapist who has over nineteen years of experience in the mental health field. She is currently the Chief Executive Officer of Airport Marina Counseling Service (AMCS)— a nonprofit, community-based mental health clinic in California.
talk_about: How to tell if you're in a healthy or unhealthy relationship
The link between abusive relationships & anxiety and depression
Questions you need to ask yourself about your relationship
Risk factors that someone could end up in an unhealthy relationship
How to set boundaries in a relationship
What to do if your partner is unreceptive to your boundaries
Ways to help someone who's in an unhealthy relationship
Tips on how parents should talk to teens about relationships

+ AMCS's Website

+ Love is Respect

guests: eden garcia-balis, licensed marriage and family therapist and ceo of airport marina counseling service
summary: sadie talks with eden garcia-balis, a therapist and ceo of a nonprofit mental health clinic, about navigating unhealthy relationships as a teen. they cover how to recognize red flags (controlling behavior, isolation, disrespect), why teens are vulnerable to unhealthy dynamics (family history, lack of self-awareness, glamorization in media), and practical steps to take if you're in one—including having tough conversations, setting boundaries, and knowing when to involve friends, parents, or professionals. eden also discusses healing after leaving an abusive relationship: journaling, self-reflection, therapy, and rebuilding self-esteem before dating again. listeners learn specific questions to ask themselves about what they want in a partner and how communication, respect, and equal footing define a healthy relationship.
quote: if you're already thinking, this is going to get my partner mad, that's a red flag.
quote_display: if you're ALREADY thinking, this is going to get my partner MAD, that's a RED FLAG.
